sample_unit: datasets (two EEG datasets: Alzheimer's disease and epileptic seizures) plus literature survey

links.outcome: Test accuracy under segment-based (leaky) versus subject-based holdout in EEG DNN classifiers
links.effect: In both the Alzheimer's and seizure datasets, performance on previously-unseen subjects was strongly overestimated with segment-based holdout compared with subject-based holdout; most surveyed translational DNN-EEG studies use segment-based holdout.
links.quote: In both datasets, we find that performance on previously-unseen subjects is strongly overestimated when models are trained using segment-based holdout.

screen.practice: subject-based holdout validation (evaluation on unseen subjects)
screen.reason: Empirically demonstrates the impact of data leakage (segment-based vs subject-based holdout validation) on diagnostic EEG deep learning performance across two clinical datasets.
